paper_id: ERA-CoT_ Improving Chain-of-Thought through Entity Relationship Analysis__oa_W4402671544
title: ERA-CoT: Improving Chain-of-Thought through Entity Relationship Analysis
motivation: LLMs struggle with complex multi-entity scenarios due to implicit relationships requiring multi-step reasoning.
problem_framing: Decompose CoT reasoning into entity extraction, explicit/implicit relationship analysis, and relationship discrimination.
key_insight: Filtering unreliable implicit relationships via scoring threshold eliminates erroneous relations that otherwise degrade reasoning.
method_signature: Five-step ERA-CoT pipeline: entity extraction, explicit RE, implicit inference, discrimination scoring, Q&A.
evaluation_criteria: Accuracy (EM) on 6 datasets across commonsense, logical, and mathematical reasoning.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Performance improvement is not significant for tasks with fewer entity relationships like symbolic reasoning.
evidence_for_taste: implicit relationship inference is prone to errors
A reasonable number of implicit relationships contributes to a better understanding
excessively large number may lead to hallucinations
If the relationships are correctly inferred, the model is likely to answer questions correctly
Small LLMs still possess the ability to identify implicit relationships
thinking_moves: Identify that CoT fails on implicit entity relations, then decompose the problem into extractable sub-tasks
Use Self-Consistency to filter noisy NER and relation extraction outputs
Decompose relationship inference into explicit (directly stated) and implicit (multi-hop) components
Apply ablation to discover which step contributes most to failure (implicit inference errors dominate)
Tune k (number of implicit relations) to balance capability gain vs hallucination risk
Set threshold v_th to eliminate low-confidence inferred relations rather than forcing all into reasoning
